title: mcw-1999-midwestern-heavyweight
label: Mr. Fantastic

won.source: Won an eight-man tournament final by pinfall to become the first champion.

note: The record does not extend past this pay-per-view far enough to confirm whether this reign continued; a later broadcast shows another wrestler holding a title on camera without naming which one.

title: mcw-1999-television
label: Ricky "The Grinder" Grant

won.source: Recorded as the reigning champion in the promotion's own rankings as of early April 1999; retained the title at the pay-per-view later that month in a match wagering his own freedom against the challenger's legal case.

note: The title later changes hands off-record; a different wrestler is recorded holding it by August 1999.

title: mcw-1999-television
label: Nicklaus Kain

won.source: Recorded as the reigning champion in the promotion's own broadcast of 13 August 1999; the record does not capture how the title changed hands from the previous champion.

note: Set to defend against the promotion's own number-one contender in a match scheduled beyond the end of this record.

title: mcw-1999-light-heavyweight
label: "Wildcat" Jim Lewis, Jr.

won.source: Recorded as the reigning champion in the promotion's own rankings as of early April 1999.

note: His title defense at the April 1999 pay-per-view ended with an apparently manufactured pinfall attempt by an interfering rival; the broadcast declares no clear result, so no change of title is recorded here.

won.source: Won the deciding round-robin tag tournament match by pinfall to become the first champions.

title: mcw-1999-gladiator
label: "Superstar" Sean Cage

won.source: Recorded as the reigning champion in the promotion's own broadcast of 13 August 1999; the title's own introduction and this reign's own start are not captured in this record.

note: Set to defend in a rematch, in a best-of-three-falls match, beyond the end of this record.
